Bookkeeping · holistic re-evaluation · walk and stage ladder

Bookkeeping, built right

You said Bookkeeping has too much scrolling, the Ledger doesn't show enough, and there's no running balance, and that you want it built right rather than patched. This hub walks the built tool at desktop and phone widths and measures each place. It then names what keeps going wrong, lays out a new set of stages, and draws the screens those stages lead to. The first tab is the walk; mark it up, then use the last tab to paste your answers back.

STATION 1

Overview

Does it orient you in one screen? On a desktop it nearly does. On a phone the real content starts below the fold, and on both it describes what you recorded, not where your money stands.

MeasuredDesktopPhone
Page length993px · 1.1 screens2,072px · 2.5 screens
Page heading + tabs, before anything else282px427px (51% of the screen); the 5 tabs wrap onto 3 lines
First figure421px577px
“Needs your attention” heading553px917px, below the 844px fold

What works

  • The pairing is right: what needs your attention beside what you did recently, and every row opens its record.
  • On a desktop it fits in about one screen.

What gets in the way

  • A large page title the rest of the console doesn't use, repeated on every view.
  • The figures answer “how much did I record”, not “where does the money stand”.
  • The spend figure has no period.
  • On a phone, five tabs take three lines.

What I'd change

  • Open on a money band: business account, card owing, owed to you, and this month's spend (Q1).
  • The console's standard header, with Add expense on the tab row (Q2).
  • Four tabs, with Needs attention folded into this page and the Expenses filter (Q3).

Q1Overview opens on where the money stands, then what needs your attention

Recommend: Reshape. A joined band, in this order: business account balance, card owing, owed to you, and spent this month compared with last. Below it, “Needs attention” and “Recent” as compact tables.

What rides on it: the first three figures need Stage 2 (accounts and opening balances). Until then the band shows only the spend tile, with its month named.

Drawn: Drawn › Overview

Q2The console's standard header, with tabs and Add expense on one row

Recommend: Reshape. A 20px title with the eyebrow, then one tab row with + Add expense at its right end. The heading drops from 282px to about 130px on a desktop and from 427px to about 150px on a phone. Each view's own repeated heading block (“Expenses / Add an expense / Record the purchase once…”) goes.

What rides on it: nothing else; this is the single biggest scroll saving on every view.

Q3Needs attention stops being its own tab

Recommend: Reshape. It already appears three times: on Overview, as its own tab, and as a stub on Reports. Keep it on Overview, and add a Needs attention filter with its amber count on Expenses (the count also rides on the Expenses tab). That leaves four tabs: Overview · Expenses · Ledger · Reports, which fit one line on a phone.

What rides on it: the phone tab row fitting one line; the worklist stays one tap from Overview.

STATION 2

Expenses list and Add an expense

Where does “too much scrolling” come from? I measured it rather than guessed. About half of it is the frame above the first field, which repeats on every view. Most of the rest is that Save sits at the bottom of a page instead of the foot of a window. The fields themselves are normal height.

What works

  • The fields are the right ones, in words an owner uses; CAD takes one amount.
  • A missing receipt is allowed and followed up.
  • Leaving with unsaved changes asks first.
  • A save error jumps to the field it names.

What gets in the way

  • The frame before the first field: 464px on a desktop, 677px on a phone.
  • Save scrolls away; no window keeps it in reach.
  • A tall text box for a one-line answer.
  • Two 23px checkboxes on a phone.
  • The list stacks facts that belong in columns.
  • Voided entries show by default.
  • Reload or Back loses your place.

What I'd change

  • Add and Correct open in the shared window, with Save pinned (Q4).
  • Expenses becomes a table, with active entries by default (Q5).
  • Copy-as-new, a duplicate warning and search by amount come with it (Q6).
  • Each view gets its own address (Q16).

Q4Add an expense and Correct open in the product's shared window

Recommend: Reshape. A 640px window over the list, two fields to a row, with Save pinned in the foot so it is always on screen. On a phone it fills the screen with ← in the corner. “What was it for?” becomes one line. More details stays collapsed but shows its current values in one line (“Tax unknown · 100% business · no notes”), so you can see them without opening it. The window's built-in “Keep writing / Discard” replaces today's hand-made one.

What rides on it: scroll to Save drops to 0 in every case. Correct and Void move into windows too (Q15).

Drawn: Drawn › Expenses and Add

Q5Expenses becomes a table

Recommend: Reshape. Columns: Date · Supplier · What for · Category · Paid from · Receipt · Amount, in the console's table style, about 30px a row (about 20 rows per desktop screen instead of 4). One toolbar: Find · Period · Category · Paid from · Status (Active by default) · the amber Needs-attention filter · Export, and the total for what's showing. On a phone each row becomes a card.

What rides on it: the Reports drill-down lists use the same table.

Q6Copy-as-new, a duplicate warning and search by amount ride in Stage 1

Recommend: include them. All three were on the accountant review's list. They belong to the same entry screen, and they're cheap once the window exists. Find matches “18.08” as well as names. A record has Copy as new for the monthly repeats. The form warns, without blocking, when the same supplier and amount already exist within 7 days.

Q16Each view gets its own web address

Recommend: Reshape. Overview, Expenses, Ledger and Reports, plus an open record, each get an address. Reload keeps your place, Back works, and a link from the console's Today page can land on the exact record.

STATION 3

US-dollar purchases

Ruled at the start of this session: two amounts in, rate shown. What's left is how you say where the CAD figure came from.

What works

  • It already stores both the original and the CAD amount; nothing is guessed.

What gets in the way

  • Conversion lives only in a free-text sentence.
  • You retype the same source every time.

What I'd change

  • Two amounts and a rate line: “1 USD = 1.4064 CAD, from your two amounts”, stored with the entry (ruled).
  • “Where the CAD figure came from” becomes a pick list, with the free-text note optional (Q7).

Q7“Where the CAD figure came from” becomes a pick list

Recommend: Reshape. A dropdown with Card statement · Bank statement · Bank of Canada rate · Invoice shows CAD, defaulting to the last one you used for that payment source, plus an optional note. Older entries keep their sentence as the note.

What rides on it: the Needs-attention reason “USD conversion evidence needed” becomes precise: it means no source was picked.

Drawn: Drawn › Expenses and Add, USD specimen

STATION 4

The Ledger

“The ledger does not display enough information, there is no running balance.” Both are true, and the second one points at a bigger gap than the screen itself.

Per row todayWhat a set of books shows (club and team ledgers already do)
Name · date · kind · “Money in/out/Paid personally” · amountDate · What · Category · Money out · Money in · Balance after this line, between a starting-balance row and an ending-balance row
No accountWhich account the money moved in (bank, card, you)
No filters, no period, no totalsType · Status · Date filters; the balance figure in the toolbar
Record opens as a card above the list, with an empty “Reason for voiding” box and a red Void always showingThe row opens a record window; Void is a question you choose to ask

The widening: real books don't have to wait for Stripe

The plan holds the ledger back until the Stripe income contract settles. But you have no live charges yet, so today nothing moves the business's money outside this tool, with two small exceptions it can't record yet: paying off the card, and bank interest or a supplier refund.

The opening balance from a statement, plus money you put in, minus money you took out, expenses paid from that account and paybacks, is the account's balance. A statement tick-off proves it to the cent. The development books already show it: $100 in, $50 out, $18.08 out on the card.

Only Stripe income (sales, fees, refunds, payouts) has to wait. It must land before the first live charge; after that, an untracked payout would make the balance silently wrong.

What works

  • Owner money is its own kind of record, kept apart from the purchase it repays.
  • A linked expense can't be voided before its payback.
  • Corrections keep their history.

What gets in the way

  • It mixes money from different places, so nothing sums.
  • No opening balance.
  • The first row is below the fold on a phone.
  • Void is always open on a transfer.

What I'd change

  • One register per account, with a running balance (Q8). Which accounts depends on your answer to Q9.
  • Two more kinds of line: move between accounts, other money in (Q10).
  • Statement tick-off and “closed through” on the register itself (Q11).

Q8The Ledger becomes one register per account, with a running balance

Recommend: Reshape. An account picker (Business chequing · Business card · Owed to you), then the club ledger's recipe: Date · What · Kind · Money out · Money in · Balance, between Starting and Ending balance rows, with the balance in the toolbar. Owed to you is a register too: personally paid purchases add to it and paybacks take it down. That's the “owner balance” from the accountant review.

What rides on it: every expense needs an account. “How did you pay?” already says which (Business bank / Business card / Paid personally); each choice becomes an account. Opening balances come from your statements.

Drawn: Drawn › Ledger

Q9Which accounts does the business actually pay from? (tick all that apply; this is the business-account decision R10 was waiting for)

This decides the registers. If you pay some things on a personal card, those stay “Paid personally” and land in Owed to you, not in a register of their own.

Q10Two new kinds of line: Move between accounts and Other money in

Recommend: Reshape. Paying the card from chequing is neither an expense nor owner money; without it the card's balance never comes down. Bank interest and a supplier's refund are money in that isn't a sale. Neither is income from customers, so neither needs Stripe.

Q11Statement tick-off and “closed through” live on the register

Recommend: Reshape. A tick column: you tick each line against the statement, and the register shows “Ticked to statement through Oct 14”. Closing a month marks “Closed through Oct 31”. A later entry dated inside a closed month warns and asks for a reason. Closing October is the event that now switches on the console's S9a signal. Ticks and closes are new records, like everything else here, so the database stays add-only.

STATION 5

Reports

“Not robust”, in your words today: month by month, money position, a tax-time statement, and compare one period with another. Today there's one long page answering one question: what did I spend in this period?

MeasuredDesktopPhone

SectionsDates to review · By category · By supplier · Purchase tax · By payment source · Entries · Paid personally · Needs attention · USD invoices

What works (keep it)

  • Every figure opens the entries behind it, and the exports follow what's on screen.
  • Every figure names its period.
  • The accountant package (CSV, receipts, hashes) is solid.

What gets in the way

  • No months side by side, so no trend.
  • No comparison.
  • Worklist and personal-payment stubs repeat what other tabs own.
  • No summary page (R5, decided, unbuilt).

What I'd change

  • Five views, picked from one View pill: Spending (today's, tidied) · By month · Compare · Money position · Tax year (Q12).
  • The tax-year statement laid out by the T2125 lines, through a mapping you confirm once (Q13).
  • The package's first page is that statement (Q14).

Q12Reports becomes five views, picked from one View pill

Recommend: Reshape. Spending (today's report, tidied: by category and supplier with drill-down), By month (categories down, months across, each cell opens its entries), Compare (this period beside the last, with the change), Money position (each account's balance and owed-to-you on a date), and Tax year. Each opens in the period you last used.

What rides on it: Money position needs Stage 2's accounts; the other three only need data the tool already has.

Drawn: Drawn › Reports

Q13The tax-year statement uses the self-employment form's lines (T2125), through a mapping you confirm once

Recommend: Reshape, with two catches. Each category points at one T2125 line (Software → 8810 Office expenses, Advertising → 8521, and so on). You confirm the mapping once, and the statement shows which category fed each line. It keeps the earlier ruling that a category is an entry aid: the mapping is yours and visible, not an automatic answer.
Catch 1: “Travel & meals” has to split into Travel and Meals, because meals are generally only half claimable. Catch 2: a large equipment purchase, like a laptop, is usually depreciated (capital cost allowance) rather than claimed in one year, so the statement flags it instead of adding it in.

Q14The accountant package's first page (R5) is the period's statement

Recommend: Reshape. The summary R5 asked for is the Tax year view (or the chosen period) with the money position and the open-items count, as page one of the ZIP. One source, so the package and the screen can't disagree.

STATION 6

The expense record: correct and void

Walked and passed (§382, §383). Its contents stay. What changes is its shape, now that the screens around it change shape, and that shape turns out to cause one of your open rulings.

The void form is the cause of BKX-5.9

You ruled that a void must keep the entry's own values. Today it doesn't, and the measurement shows why: Void reuses the whole correction form, every field editable, so a void can carry changed amounts and dates.

Make Void what the plan always said it was, a separate question with one field (the reason), and there's nothing else to change. The fix and the reshape are the same piece of work.

The same applies to a transfer, where today the void form sits open on the record.

Q15A record opens as a window over its list; Void becomes a small question

Recommend: Reshape. Click a row and the record window opens over the list, reading first. The pencil flips the whole record into the correction form, which asks why at Save. The record ends with Copy as new and Void this expense…; its foot steps to the next or previous entry in the list. Your call: each correction writes a permanent revision with its reason, so I'd hold a correction until ✓ rather than autosave it as other records do. Void opens a 416px question: what leaves your totals, that the values stay exactly as entered, and the reason. Transfers get the same.

What rides on it: BKX-5.9 closes by construction, and its server rule (refuse a void whose values differ from the latest version) is built alongside.

Drawn: Drawn › Record and Void

STATION 8

Formatting

Already ruled (BKX-5.10): Bookkeeping takes the console's lettering. No question here; it's placed in Stage 1.

What's measured

  • Tabs, buttons, labels, inputs and figures in the typewriter face.
  • Dates print as 2026-10-27; the house format is Oct 27, 2026.
  • Square, lime-outlined fields.

Placed

  • All three go into Stage 1, so every reshaped screen is drawn in the console's real look (as in the Drawn tab).

Outside Bookkeeping (for the console)

  • On a phone, the console's top bar overlaps its logo and “Support console”.

Standing back: what cuts across the stations

The same few things cause most of what you named. Fix them once and each station gets better together.

1The scrolling is mostly the frame, not the fields

Before you type anything: 464px on a desktop and 677px on a phone. Every view repeats a 44px page title, the tabs, and then its own second heading. The fields are a normal 44px, about 81px a row. So the fix is the console's standard header plus the shared window with Save pinned, not squeezing fields. That takes scroll-to-Save to zero for CAD, USD, correction and void alike.

2Every form and every question opens in the shared window

Today 0 of 6 do: Add expense, Correct expense, Void expense, Add transfer, Correct transfer, Void transfer. Each is a hand-built page or inline card. Moving them gives you the window's built-in leave-without-saving guard, the phone full-screen behaviour, and the house's question shape, which is the shape that fixes BKX-5.9.

3A list that answers by column is a table

Expenses, the Ledger and the Reports drill-downs all stack facts in small grey lines. At 1440px that's 4 rows on the first screen. The console's table recipe (about 30px a row, condensed column headings, money right-aligned) shows about 20, and each fact gets a column you can scan.

4“Enough information” means the same thing everywhere

A money row shows its date, who, what kind, which account, out or in, and, on a register, the balance after it. A figure names its period and opens the rows behind it. Reports already does the second half; the Ledger does neither.

5Real books don't wait for Stripe, but Stripe can't wait for the first sale

With no live charges, every movement of the business's money is something you can enter, so registers with opening balances, running balances and a statement tick-off can be built now. Only customer income (sales, fees, refunds, payouts) needs the Revenue contract, and it has to land before the first live charge. This replaces the plan's line that the ledger waits for Revenue.

6Add-only stays add-only

The bookkeeping database lets the app read and add, never change or delete. Ticks, closes, account opening balances and the category-to-tax-line mapping are all new records with their own history, like corrections are. Nothing in this ladder asks for that permission to change.

7One look, one date format, one address per view

The console's lettering (ruled), the house dates (“Oct 27, 2026”, and “Oct 1” on a ledger row), and an address for each view, so reload, Back and a link from Today all land where you meant.

8Where I'd push back on the plan's order

The old ladder put the ledger after Revenue, and treated reports as done once figures drilled down. Both came from “expense-only first”. That made sense while income was expected first; it doesn't now. I'd also keep the GST/HST fields out of Stage 1 even though they live on the same form: they get their own session (your R3 ruling), and drawing them here would pre-empt it.

What “built right” looks like at the top of this ladder

You enter a purchase in one window without scrolling. Each account's balance matches its statement to the cent and says how far it's ticked. You can see what the business owes you, month by month spending, and what moved since last month. At tax time you hand over a statement laid out by the form's lines, with its receipts. When Stripe starts, its money lands in the same registers.

Drawn: the end state of Stages 1–3

One proposal screen per place, in the console's real look and true size. Desktop frames fit your window; press True size to see them at 1440px. Phones are always true size; open this page on your phone to judge them. Each tag says what changed and which stage delivers it; click a tag for the reason. Figures are invented examples, chosen to add up across every screen.

Ruled Oct 27. Stage 1 and Stage 3 parts stand as drawn. Parts tagged S2 assume a business chequing account and card, which your Q9 answer rules out: the chequing register, card owing, and the Overview band's first tiles. Stage 2 gets redrawn for personal-account books before it's built.
